notes: Dev-time eval set for skill authoring. Fixtures are described by SHAPE so the set is not tied to any one checkout; the `example_fixture` field points at a copy that existed in the development checkout, but a runner should supply its own equivalent. Each eval runs against a fresh COPY of its fixture (the flow writes certora/ artifacts into the project). Evals 1-2 need CERTORAKEY + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and submit real cloud prover jobs (autosetup alone runs several) — expect long wall-clock and real cost. Eval 3 is cheap and offline (fails at preflight).

evals.name: trivial-end-to-end-answer
evals.prompt: Formally verify the Answer contract at src/Answer.sol:Answer in <project> — come up with properties and prove them with the Certora prover.
evals.fixture: A tiny Foundry project whose src/Answer.sol declares `contract Answer` with a pure function returning a constant (e.g. theAnswer() => 42), optionally with a design.md describing intended behavior. No pre-existing certora/ or emv-*/ artifacts.
evals.example_fixture: smoketest/ from the development checkout (strip emv-*/ and any certora/ dir from the copy)
evals.expected_output: Full flow: finds or notes the design doc, writes certora/analysis/application.json, autosetup produces certora/confs/Answer.conf + summaries, an agent-authored per-component spec that imports BOTH Answer_base_summaries.spec AND Answer_call_resolution.spec with at least a rule that theAnswer() returns 42, a clean full certoraRun, and certora/report/report.json + report.md with every property mapped to rules and GOOD outcomes.
assertions: autosetup ran and certora/confs/Answer.conf exists in the project copy
an agent-authored component spec (i.e. NOT the autosetup-generated sanity-Answer.spec) imports BOTH the base-summaries spec AND the call-resolution spec
certora/properties/<slug>.property_rules.json was written and every formulated property appears in report.json mapped to >=1 rule with an outcome
the final certoraRun had no rule filter and all rules VERIFIED (report outcomes all GOOD)
report.md states the per-outcome counts and links the prover run(s)

evals.name: planted-bug-counter-surfaces-finding
evals.prompt: Formally verify <project> with the certora prover, main contract src/Counter.sol:Counter. I want real verification results, not just a spec.
evals.fixture: A tiny Foundry project with a Counter contract that has a KNOWN planted bug: an incrementOther(address other) function documented to credit `other` but whose body actually credits msg.sender. Any comments revealing the bug MUST be removed from the copy. Provide src/ + foundry.toml only (no certora/, no emv-*/).
evals.example_fixture: the Counter fixture in the development checkout's test scenarios (src/ + foundry.toml; strip the bug-revealing comments in Counter.sol)
evals.expected_output: Properties include per-method correctness of incrementOther (the target address is credited). The prover finds the violation (implementation credits msg.sender); the skill marks the rule expected-to-fail with reason 'genuine issue' and reports it as a finding with the counterexample scenario — it does NOT weaken the spec until the rule passes, and does NOT skip the property. A structural invariant tying count to the increments mapping is formulated.
assertions: a property about incrementOther crediting the target address exists in the properties artifact
the corresponding rule outcome is BAD/VIOLATED in report.json and is flagged as an expected failure marked 'genuine issue' (a finding), not silently removed and not marked 'prover limitation'
report.md describes the bug (credits msg.sender instead of other) as a finding for human review
no rule was made to pass by asserting the buggy behavior (spec does not assert increments[msg.sender] grows on incrementOther)
a structural invariant relating count and the increments mapping was formulated (proven or documented why not)

evals.name: preflight-fast-fail-interface-target
evals.prompt: Please formally verify Intf.sol:Intf in <project> using the certora prover — properties + proofs.
evals.fixture: A directory whose Intf.sol declares ONLY an interface (e.g. `interface Intf {}`) with no concrete contract of that name.
evals.example_fixture: examples/trivial/ from the development checkout (Intf.sol contains only `interface Intf`)
evals.expected_output: The flow stops at Phase 0 preflight with a clear explanation: the target is an interface (a concrete contract is required; autosetup rejects abstract/interface main contracts) — no fabricated specs, no fake verification claims, and a concrete suggestion (point at a concrete implementation).
assertions: no component spec or report.json claiming verification results was produced
the final message explicitly says the target is an interface/abstract and cannot be set up
no claim that any rule was verified
